evals.name: worklog-summary-from-plan-conversation
evals.context: User had a design conversation (002-summary-conversation.md) and a plan-mode document (002-summary-plan.md) for a `worklog summary` CLI command. The skill was invoked after both existed in conversation context.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained ticket with: (1) Summary capturing design decisions AND the conversation back-and-forth (human overrides, redirections), (2) Scope section with in/out/related items, (3) Plan section preserving behavioral contract (CLI output format, exit codes, sort order, empty-range semantics) not just file listings with type signatures. The ticket should not require the reader to find the plan document separately.
observations: Summary section was good — captured 6 key design decisions with rationale
Plan section distilled to file listings + type signatures, dropped behavioral contract (CLI output format, exit codes, sort rules, empty-range semantics)
No Scope section — out-of-scope items (presets, date-fns, configurable sort) buried in Summary narrative
Conversation summary thin — says 'settled in conversation' without capturing human redirections (pushed back on grouping, overrode separate-skill recommendation)
Ticket assumes plan document travels with it — not self-contained

assertions.text: Ticket contains an explicit Scope section with In Scope and Out of Scope headers
Ticket documents the behavioral contract — exit codes, output format, and edge case behavior
Conversation trail names specific human overrides — not just 'as discussed' or 'settled in conversation'
Ticket does not reference external plan documents the reader would need to find
Each out-of-scope item includes a reason for exclusion, not just a bare list
assertions.description: Review each Out of Scope item — every item should have a short rationale (e.g. 'the agent caller resolves these') not just a label

assertions.text: Ticket specifies what happens when the date range matches no entries
When a detailed plan existed in the conversation, the Execution Detail section is present and non-trivial
Related Work section references sibling tickets (001 and 003)
